```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>"
)
```

You've just received notifications that your tag matches are in, hooray!! Let's walk through how to interact with all of your data.

```{r setup}
library(otndata)
library(dplyr)
library(arrow)
```

First, we need to log in. If you have never entered your username and password before, you'll need to do so. I'm an ACT member, so I'll be logging into my network. If you're a member of a different network, just switch in your network's code. Run the following:

```{r}
otn_login("act")
```

This will just set your credentials for the current R session. If you wish to use the same credentials after closing/reopening R, use `otn_set_credentials`:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
otn_set_credentials("act")
```

It might be that you just want a high-level summary of what's new. `otndata` interfaces seamlessly with the [`otndo` package](https://otndo.obrien.page) using [`otn_receiver_summary`](https://otndata.obrien.page/reference/otn_receiver_summary.html) or [`otn_tag_summary`](https://otndata.obrien.page/reference/otn_tag_summary.html) for receiver and tag projects, respectively.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
otn_receiver_summary("tailwinds")
otn_tag_summary("mdbsb")
```

After this, you might want to dig a little further into all of the data extract files on offer.

```{r}
otn_extract_files(project = "tailwinds")
```

This can be a lot! We can just grab the files that have been modified after a certain date -- usually the date just before the most-recent data push.

```{r}
otn_extract_files(project = "tailwinds", since = "2026-07-28")
```

The most important thing, however, is downloading those files! Let's grab the parquet files via `otn_extract_files`, download them with `otn_download`, and create a mini-database for ourselves.

```{r}
otn_extract_files(
  project = "tailwinds",
  text = "mapped parquet",
  since = "2026-07-28"
) |>
  otn_download(outdir = "./my_awesome_detections")
```

Create a database on the fly using the [arrow package](https://arrow.apache.org/docs/r).

```{r}
my_db <- arrow::open_dataset("my_awesome_detections/")
my_db
```

Now we can do some really quick summaries.

```{r}
my_db |>
  dplyr::group_by(trackerCode) |>
  dplyr::tally() |>
  dplyr::arrange(-n) |>
  dplyr::collect()
```

Or find out who we should email and say "hi!".

```{r}
my_db |>
  dplyr::distinct(contactPI) |>
  dplyr::mutate(contactPI = sub(" \\(.*", "", contactPI)) |>
  head() |>
  dplyr::collect()
```




```{r, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# Clean up the folder made above
rm(my_db)
unlink("my_awesome_detections", recursive = T)
```
